decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Advanced Ecological Modeling
decks.description: Develop advanced ecological process and observation models.

includes: Stochastic population and spatial ecological processes
Hierarchical observation models and ecological uncertainty

practice: Implement a process-observation ecological model and test inference on synthetic and field datasets.

outcomes.description: Derive hierarchical abundance/occupancy likelihoods and assess parameter, observation and process uncertainty.
Implement spatial dispersal and reaction models and assess discretization and scale dependence.
Construct and analyze stochastic population models and distinguish demographic from environmental variability.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Animal Physiology
decks.description: Explain integrated animal function and physiological failure.

includes: Comparative homeostasis, circulation, respiration, digestion and excretion
Neural/endocrine regulation, movement and reproduction

practice: Interpret physiological traces and calculate compartment/flow balances for normal and perturbed systems.

outcomes.description: Analyze physiological feedback loops and distinguish compensation from restoration of normal function.
Explain electrical excitability, synapses, muscle activation and endocrine regulation at a qualitative mechanistic level.
Explain gametogenesis, reproductive endocrine cycles and comparative reproductive strategies.
Apply locally taught flow, diffusion and clearance balances to circulation, gas exchange, digestion and excretion.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Genomics and Bioinformatics
decks.description: Implement and evaluate genomic inference workflows.

includes: Alignment, assembly and sequence-data quality
Variant, expression and genome-scale functional analysis

practice: Build a reproducible public-data workflow and implement core alignment/counting components with validation cases.

outcomes.description: Analyze count-based expression and functional enrichment using locally taught count models and multiple-testing controls.
Construct variant-analysis workflows and interpret mapping, population and annotation biases.
Implement alignment and elementary assembly methods and assess sequencing-error and repeat ambiguity.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Cell Biology
decks.description: Relate cellular organization to function and regulation.

includes: Cell architecture, membranes, organelles and cytoskeleton
Transport, signaling, trafficking, cell cycle and apoptosis

practice: Interpret microscopy and perturbation datasets to distinguish competing cellular mechanisms.

outcomes.description: Explain cell-cycle checkpoints, chromosome segregation and programmed cell death and predict failure consequences.
Interpret cell images and relate organelles, cytoskeleton and trafficking to compartmental function.
Trace receptor-to-response signaling and predict qualitative effects of pathway perturbations.
Explain membrane selectivity, diffusion, osmosis and active transport using qualitative electrochemical gradients.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Community and Population Ecology
decks.description: Develop working methods for populations and communities.

includes: Population/community dynamics and stability
Diversity, interaction inference and spatial sampling/modeling

practice: Analyze community data and compare fitted interaction models with experimental or temporal predictions.

outcomes.description: Estimate diversity and interaction effects while accounting for sampling and competing causal explanations.
Derive and analyze growth, competition and consumer-resource ODE models.
Construct metapopulation and spatial sampling models and diagnose scale and detection biases.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Conservation Biology
decks.description: Translate ecological evidence into conservation decisions.

includes: Population viability, fragmentation and genetic risk
Reserve design, restoration, adaptive management and decision uncertainty

practice: Use a supplied viability simulator and ecological evidence to defend and critique a management plan.

outcomes.description: Compare habitat, connectivity and genetic-management interventions under explicit objectives and tradeoffs.
Construct deterministic and locally specified stochastic viability projections and assess extinction-risk sensitivity.
Design restoration monitoring and adaptive decisions with counterfactual and uncertainty considerations.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Developmental Biology
decks.description: Explain how cells construct and repair organisms.

includes: Fate specification, induction and gene-regulatory patterning
Morphogenesis, stem cells, regeneration and evolutionary development

practice: Reconstruct developmental mechanisms from lineage, imaging and perturbation datasets.

outcomes.description: Distinguish specification, determination and differentiation using lineage and transplantation evidence.
Explain positional information and regulatory patterning and predict perturbation phenotypes.
Relate cell mechanics, growth and signaling to morphogenesis, regeneration and developmental evolution.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Ecology
decks.description: An accessible entry to organisms in their environments.

includes: Environmental limits and ecological sampling
Discrete demography, interactions, food webs and ecosystem budgets

practice: Analyze a local or supplied ecological survey and construct a demographic and ecosystem accounting model.

outcomes.description: Explain competition, predation, mutualism and trophic structure using testable predictions.
Design simple quadrat/transect sampling and interpret abundance, occupancy and detection limitations.
Construct elementary energy and nutrient budgets and distinguish stocks from flows.
Construct life tables and discrete population-growth projections.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Ecosystem Science
decks.description: Quantify ecosystem processes across coupled compartments.

includes: Carbon, nutrient and water budgets across ecosystems
Microbial/physical coupling, productivity and global-change responses

practice: Reconcile an ecosystem flux dataset with a mass-balanced compartment model and perturbation scenarios.

outcomes.description: Construct and check carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus and water compartment budgets.
Model coupled productivity, decomposition and nutrient limitations using explicit biological and chemical assumptions.
Interpret ecosystem responses to climate and land-use perturbations with uncertainty and scale limits.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Epidemiology
decks.description: Infer population-health patterns and intervention effects.

includes: Incidence, prevalence, survival and observational study designs
Causal diagrams, confounding and bias
Locally taught compartmental transmission models

practice: Appraise a cohort study and compare transmission scenarios without interpreting model output as clinical advice.

outcomes.description: Use locally introduced causal diagrams and study designs to identify confounding, selection and measurement bias.
Calculate risk, rate, odds and survival measures and distinguish their sampling interpretations.
Derive elementary compartmental transmission models and calculate threshold and intervention effects.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Evolutionary Biology
decks.description: Explain evolutionary change using mechanisms and evidence.

includes: Selection, drift, migration and mutation
Speciation, phylogenetic evidence, adaptation and evolutionary constraints

practice: Evaluate evolutionary explanations using trait, population and fossil datasets rather than adaptation narratives alone.

outcomes.description: Interpret phylogenetic and fossil evidence and distinguish homology, convergence and adaptive explanations.
Calculate elementary allele-frequency updates and distinguish selection, drift, migration and mutation signatures.
Compare reproductive-isolation mechanisms and evaluate speciation evidence.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Evolutionary Theory and Phylogenetics
decks.description: Infer evolutionary histories using explicit stochastic models.

includes: Coalescent and diffusion approximations
Substitution models, phylogenetic likelihood and evolutionary model comparison

practice: Implement a small phylogenetic likelihood engine and compare evolutionary explanations for public sequence data.

outcomes.description: Derive elementary coalescent waiting times and connect diffusion/coalescent approximations to finite populations.
Compare demographic, selection and trait-evolution models and diagnose nonidentifiability and model misspecification.
Implement tree-likelihood pruning under substitution models and evaluate phylogenetic uncertainty.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Biological Experimental Methods
decks.description: Establish reusable biological laboratory methods.

includes: Biological experimental design and reproducibility
Microscopy, sterile culture and measurement
Extraction, PCR, gels, immunoassays and controls taught operationally

practice: Complete a supervised low-risk assay study with controls, raw images, dilution records and reproducible analysis.

outcomes.description: Design biological experiments with controls, randomization, replication and explicit measurement endpoints.
Perform or interpret calibrated microscopy and nonpathogenic culture using sterile technique and counting methods.
Plan extraction, PCR, electrophoresis and immunoassay workflows using locally taught reagent and signal principles.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Genetics
decks.description: Infer inheritance mechanisms from genetic evidence.

includes: Mendelian/non-Mendelian inheritance, meiosis and pedigrees
Linkage, recombination, chromosome variation and genetic tests

practice: Solve unfamiliar pedigree and mapping datasets and state unresolved genetic alternatives.

outcomes.description: Explain chromosome-number/structure changes and interpret their inheritance consequences.
Infer inheritance models from crosses and pedigrees with penetrance and probability explicitly handled.
Estimate linkage and construct genetic maps from recombination data.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Immunology
decks.description: Explain immune protection and immune-mediated failure.

includes: Innate recognition, antigen presentation and lymphocyte diversity
Adaptive responses, memory, tolerance and immune pathology

practice: Interpret immunological perturbation and assay datasets and compare competing immune-failure mechanisms.

outcomes.description: Trace lymphocyte activation, effector differentiation and memory and interpret response assays.
Explain tolerance failure, allergy, immunodeficiency and immune evasion from mechanistic evidence.
Explain innate recognition, antigen processing and receptor-diversity mechanisms.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Infectious Disease Biology
decks.description: Explain infection as a host-pathogen interaction.

includes: Bacterial, viral, fungal and parasitic infection life cycles
Virulence, host response, resistance and intervention mechanisms

practice: Analyze supplied infection and resistance datasets and propose safe, nonclinical mechanism tests.

outcomes.description: Explain colonization, invasion, virulence and host damage using causal experimental evidence.
Compare major pathogen life cycles, transmission opportunities and tissue tropism.
Explain antimicrobial resistance and vaccine/drug mechanisms and predict biological failure modes.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Living Systems
decks.description: An accessible conceptual entry to biological science.

includes: Cells, organisms, populations and ecosystems
Energy/matter/information distinctions and biological evidence
Evolution, common ancestry and adaptation

practice: Construct evidence-based explanations from organism observations and critique competing biological claims.

outcomes.description: Distinguish observation, hypothesis, controlled comparison and causal evidence in biological examples.
Explain common ancestry and natural selection without teleological or individual-change misconceptions.
Compare biological organization and explain matter, energy and information flow using qualitative molecular language.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Microbiology
decks.description: Explain microbial function beyond disease examples.

includes: Microbial growth and environmental tolerance
Metabolic diversity, horizontal transfer, viruses and microbial communities

practice: Interpret nonpathogenic growth, enrichment and community datasets and design discriminating culture conditions.

outcomes.description: Analyze microbial interactions, biofilms and biogeochemical roles using community evidence.
Explain horizontal gene transfer, phage cycles and genetic exchange experiments.
Calculate growth and viable counts and distinguish growth limitation, death and culturability.
Compare microbial energy/carbon strategies and predict growth from environmental electron donors and acceptors.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Molecular Biology
decks.description: Explain information processing through molecular mechanisms.

includes: Replication, recombination and repair
Transcription, RNA processing, translation and gene regulation

practice: Interpret repair, reporter and expression experiments and propose targeted tests of regulatory models.

outcomes.description: Trace transcription, RNA processing and translation and interpret mechanism-discriminating experiments.
Analyze chromatin, transcriptional and post-transcriptional regulation using causal perturbation evidence.
Explain genome replication, recombination and repair and predict effects of specific molecular defects.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Neuroscience and Behavior
decks.description: Connect neural mechanisms to circuits and behavior.

includes: Membrane conductance models, synapses and plasticity
Sensory/motor circuits, learning and behavioral experiments

practice: Analyze electrophysiological and behavioral datasets and solve simplified membrane/circuit models.

outcomes.description: Design and interpret behavioral/neural experiments while distinguishing correlation, intervention and reverse inference.
Explain circuit coding, sensory/motor transformations and plasticity using physiological evidence.
Derive passive-membrane and locally specified conductance models and analyze spike-generation dynamics.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Organismal Diversity
decks.description: Organize life's diversity through comparative evidence.

includes: Phylogenetic trees and comparative characters
Bacteria, archaea, protists, fungi, plants and animals across life cycles and forms

practice: Build a character-based identification key and defend a comparative classification using specimens or images.

outcomes.description: Compare microbial, protist and fungal organization, reproduction and ecological roles.
Read rooted/unrooted trees and distinguish clades, grades and misleading similarity.
Compare major plant and animal body plans, life cycles and evolutionary innovations.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Pathobiology
decks.description: Explain disease through failed biological mechanisms.

includes: Cell injury, inflammation, degeneration and tissue repair
Inherited molecular disease and multistep cancer evolution

practice: Construct mechanism-based explanations from supplied histological, genetic and physiological case evidence.

outcomes.description: Explain oncogenic signaling, genome instability, clonal selection and tumor microenvironment effects.
Connect genetic variants to molecular dysfunction and variable organismal phenotypes without deterministic overinterpretation.
Distinguish reversible injury, death, inflammation, degeneration and repair using tissue and molecular evidence.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Plant Biology
decks.description: Connect plant form with resource acquisition and development.

includes: Plant tissues, meristems and reproductive organization
Water/mineral transport, photosynthesis, hormones and environmental responses

practice: Analyze plant water-status and photosynthetic-response experiments and identify anatomical adaptations.

outcomes.description: Predict hormone, light and stress responses and explain reproductive developmental transitions.
Interpret plant anatomy and relate tissues and meristems to growth and reproduction.
Explain water/mineral transport and carbon allocation and interpret resource-limitation experiments.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Population and Quantitative Genetics
decks.description: Model genetic variation within and between populations.

includes: Selection/mutation/migration recursions and finite-population drift
Linkage disequilibrium, quantitative inheritance and population-data inference

practice: Derive population recursions and analyze genotype/phenotype datasets with explicit model checks.

outcomes.description: Derive allele-frequency recursions and analyze equilibrium and local stability under selection and migration.
Construct finite Wright-Fisher models and calculate elementary drift, fixation and effective-size consequences.
Estimate linkage disequilibrium and population differentiation and assess demographic/selection confounding.
Partition phenotypic variance and predict selection response while distinguishing heritability from immutability.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Structural Biology
decks.description: Infer biomolecular structures from incomplete measurements.

includes: Fourier structural representations and inverse problems taught locally
Diffraction, cryo-EM and biomolecular NMR workflows
Refinement, resolution and structural validation

practice: Reconstruct a synthetic density from projections and critically validate a public biomolecular structure.

outcomes.description: Derive elementary Fourier diffraction/projection relations and explain phase and reconstruction ambiguity.
Compare crystallographic, cryo-EM and NMR restraints, sample requirements and inferential limitations.
Use provided reconstruction/refinement software and independently assess resolution, overfitting, geometry and uncertainty.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Synthetic Biology
decks.description: Engineer and evaluate bounded biological functions.

includes: Genetic circuit specification and feedback design
Assembly, host context, characterization, burden and containment

practice: Design and simulate a genetic circuit and, when authorized, characterize a nonpathogenic contained implementation.

outcomes.description: Plan sequence assembly and host integration with locally taught cloning strategies and verification controls.
Characterize circuit performance, burden, evolutionary instability and containment assumptions.
Design genetic logic and feedback circuits from explicit dynamical specifications.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Systems Biology
decks.description: Build and test quantitative models of molecular networks.

includes: Biochemical network dynamics and stoichiometric constraints
Parameter inference, identifiability, sensitivity and perturbation design

practice: Implement a biochemical network, fit time-course data and design a discriminating perturbation experiment.

outcomes.description: Construct stoichiometric and kinetic network models and analyze conservation, steady states and stability.
Estimate parameters and assess structural/practical identifiability with sensitivity and profile methods.
Design perturbations that discriminate network mechanisms and propagate model uncertainty to predictions.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Analytical Chemistry
decks.description: Design trustworthy quantitative chemical measurements.

includes: Gravimetry and titrimetric methods
Calibration, detection limits, uncertainty, validation and sampling

practice: Validate an assay with blanks, spikes, standards and an explicit uncertainty and sampling budget.

outcomes.description: Construct calibration and validation plans and calculate detection limits and measurement uncertainty.
Design and calculate gravimetric, acid-base, redox and complexometric determinations.
Design representative sampling and diagnose matrix effects, contamination and chemical interference.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Biochemistry
decks.description: Explain biological function through molecular chemistry.

includes: Proteins, nucleic acids, carbohydrates, lipids and folding
Enzyme kinetics, energy coupling and metabolic regulation

practice: Analyze enzyme data with supplied fitting tools and reconcile isotope/carbon balances through metabolism.

outcomes.description: Calculate coupled reaction free energies and explain redox and membrane-gradient energy conversion.
Relate biomolecular architecture, noncovalent interactions and folding to molecular function.
Derive elementary enzyme saturation from a stated steady-state balance and interpret inhibition plots.
Trace carbon, electrons and regulation through central catabolic and biosynthetic networks.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Quantities
decks.description: Translate chemical representations into conserved quantities.

includes: Chemical formulas, balanced reactions and moles
Concentrations, dilutions, yields and ideal-gas calculations

practice: Prepare calculation sheets for reaction batches and serial dilutions with independent mass-balance checks.

outcomes.description: Balance reactions and calculate composition, limiting reagents and yields using mole ratios.
Calculate solution concentrations, dilution plans and ideal-gas quantities with units.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Structure Foundations
decks.description: An accessible molecular language for matter.

includes: Elements, atoms, ions, periodic trends and qualitative energy levels
Lewis bonding, molecular shape and intermolecular forces

practice: Build molecular models and explain contrasting material properties without numerical quantum calculations.

outcomes.description: Interpret atomic composition, ions and periodic trends using qualitative electron-shell models.
Construct Lewis structures and predict geometry, bond polarity and resonance alternatives.
Explain phase, solubility and molecular-recognition trends through intermolecular interactions.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Computational Electronic Structure
decks.description: Implement and critically use electronic-structure methods.

includes: Basis sets and self-consistent-field algorithms
Correlation, density functionals and property validation

practice: Implement a toy Hartree-Fock solver and benchmark package calculations against controlled reference cases.

outcomes.description: Derive basic correlation corrections and explain density-functional approximations and their failure modes.
Design geometry/property calculations and separate numerical, basis and model errors.
Implement a small-basis self-consistent-field calculation with convergence and basis diagnostics.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Coordination Chemistry
decks.description: Model transition-metal structure and reactivity.

includes: Coordination geometry, isomerism and electron counting
Crystal/ligand-field matrix models, spectra, magnetism and substitution

practice: Analyze coordination spectra and kinetic evidence without claiming ab initio electronic accuracy.

outcomes.description: Distinguish coordination substitution and electron-transfer mechanisms using experimental evidence.
Assign coordination geometry, isomers, oxidation states and electron counts.
Diagonalize locally constructed ligand-field matrices and predict spin, magnetism and spectral trends.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Electrochemistry
decks.description: Connect interfacial thermodynamics with electrochemical rates.

includes: Electrochemical potentials, double layers and electrode equilibrium
Charge transfer, diffusion and device polarization

practice: Derive chronoamperometric and polarization models and compare with supplied electrochemical datasets.

outcomes.description: Analyze battery, fuel-cell and corrosion behavior through polarization, transport and efficiency balances.
Derive and solve elementary charge-transfer/diffusion models for current-voltage response.
Derive electrode equilibrium relations and explain double-layer models and reference conventions.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Environmental Chemistry
decks.description: Track chemicals through environmental systems.

includes: Air/water/soil partitioning and chemical fate
Atmospheric photochemistry, aquatic speciation and pollutant assessment

practice: Build a chemical-fate box model and evaluate a monitoring dataset without equating concentration with clinical risk.

outcomes.description: Design contaminant sampling and analytical interpretation with uncertainty and exposure boundaries.
Construct partitioning and compartment mass balances and estimate persistence and transport times.
Analyze aquatic redox/acid-base and atmospheric photochemical reaction networks using locally specified photolysis rates.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Equilibrium
decks.description: Predict composition and chemical direction at equilibrium.

includes: Mass action, reaction quotient and equilibrium balances
Acids/bases, buffers, solubility, complexes and introductory enthalpy/free energy

practice: Solve coupled speciation problems and compare approximate with numerical roots from a provided solver.

outcomes.description: Calculate pH, buffer capacity trends and titration curves for standard acid-base systems.
Solve mass-action and material-balance equations and justify approximation choices.
Use calorimetry, Hess cycles and stated free-energy relations to assess reaction favorability.
Calculate precipitation and complexation equilibria with competing species.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Inorganic Chemistry
decks.description: Explain inorganic diversity through structure and reactivity.

includes: Main-group structures, reactions and periodic trends
Oxidation states, inorganic redox and stability

practice: Construct comparative element-chemistry arguments and solve inorganic speciation/redox problems.

outcomes.description: Explain molecular, network and cluster structures using electron counting and bonding models.
Predict and compare main-group reaction patterns using bonding and periodic trends.
Balance redox chemistry and interpret oxidation-state stability using supplied potential and free-energy data.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Instrumental Analysis
decks.description: Select and interpret instrumental chemical measurements.

includes: Locally taught absorption/emission, mass-analyzer and detector models
Chromatographic separation and electroanalytical transduction

practice: Develop and compare two instrumental assays using standards and supplied or supervised instrument data.

outcomes.description: Calculate chromatographic retention, resolution and efficiency and optimize a separation.
Interpret potentiometric and voltammetric signals using locally specified electrode and diffusion models.
Explain instrument signal formation and quantify analytes using optical and mass-spectrometric measurements.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Kinetics
decks.description: Infer and model chemical rates and mechanisms.

includes: Rate laws and experimental mechanism discrimination
Reaction networks, steady-state/pre-equilibrium reductions and activation models

practice: Analyze competing kinetic models using concentration-time data and design a discriminating experiment.

outcomes.description: Analyze Arrhenius and locally specified transition-state models and distinguish kinetic from thermodynamic control.
Infer rate laws from time-course and initial-rate data with uncertainty and mechanism alternatives.
Construct mass-action ODE networks and justify steady-state and pre-equilibrium reductions.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Laboratory Methods
decks.description: Establish sound chemical bench practice.

includes: Chemical risk assessment and records
Volumetric/gravimetric preparation, extraction, filtration, distillation and purity checks

practice: Complete supervised preparation and separation exercises with notebooks, mass balances and waste records.

outcomes.description: Construct procedure-specific risk, waste and emergency plans from hazard information.
Select and execute basic separations and assess recovery and purity using locally taught checks.
Prepare and document solutions using calibrated balances and volumetric equipment with uncertainty estimates.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Materials Chemistry
decks.description: Design and characterize chemically structured solids.

includes: Crystal structures, defects and solid solutions
Reciprocal-lattice diffraction and materials synthesis routes

practice: Infer a phase mixture from diffraction and propose a synthesis/annealing strategy with defect predictions.

outcomes.description: Construct crystal and defect models and calculate charge neutrality and defect-equilibrium trends.
Index elementary powder patterns using locally taught reciprocal-lattice and structure-factor models.
Compare solid-state, solution and vapor synthesis routes using phase stability, nucleation and reaction constraints.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Molecular Simulation
decks.description: Sample molecular motion and thermodynamic observables.

includes: Force fields, molecular dynamics, constraints and thermostats
Monte Carlo, autocorrelation and free-energy methods

practice: Implement a small molecular simulation and compare ensembles, sampling diagnostics and free-energy estimates.

outcomes.description: Calculate free-energy differences with uncertainty and diagnose overlap and sampling failures.
Implement force-field dynamics with Verlet stepping and diagnose energy, constraint and thermostat behavior.
Implement Metropolis sampling and assess detailed balance, equilibration and autocorrelation.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Molecular Spectroscopy Theory
decks.description: Derive molecular spectra and their dynamical information.

includes: Molecular rotational/vibrational/electronic selection and intensities
Broadening, relaxation and time-resolved spectroscopy

practice: Derive and fit supplied steady-state and time-resolved spectra using explicitly specified response models.

outcomes.description: Relate spectral lineshapes to lifetime, collision, inhomogeneity and instrument response.
Derive transition selection rules and intensities from symmetry and transition moments.
Model time-resolved signals using state populations/coherences and assess mechanistic identifiability.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Organic Reaction Mechanisms
decks.description: Explain organic transformations through mechanisms.

includes: Substitution/elimination and alkene/alkyne additions
Aromatic and carbonyl chemistry
Radical chains and elementary pericyclic selection

practice: Solve unfamiliar product/mechanism problems and propose experiments distinguishing competing pathways.

outcomes.description: Explain addition and aromatic substitution selectivity using intermediates and electronic effects.
Construct carbonyl addition, acyl substitution and enolate mechanisms with atom/electron accounting.
Construct radical-chain mechanisms and use locally taught orbital-phase rules for elementary pericyclic reactions.
Predict substitution/elimination products and stereochemistry from substrate, reagent and solvent conditions.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Organic Structure and Reactivity Language
decks.description: Read and reason about organic molecular structure.

includes: Organic nomenclature and line representations
Stereochemistry, conformation, resonance, pKa and curved-arrow notation

practice: Construct stereochemical models and defend mechanistic arrows and acidity rankings.

outcomes.description: Translate formulas, names and line drawings and identify functional groups and constitutional isomers.
Use resonance, locally defined pKa ratios and curved arrows to justify acid-base and nucleophile/electrophile reasoning.
Assign stereochemistry and compare conformational energies using qualitative and supplied quantitative models.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Organic Synthesis
decks.description: Design and evaluate multistep molecular construction.

includes: Retrosynthesis, protecting groups and chemo/stereoselective strategy
Route feasibility, purification, yield and sustainability

practice: Defend a complete synthetic route and execute an approved small-scale segment under supervision.

outcomes.description: Generate and compare retrosynthetic disconnections for multifunctional targets.
Evaluate route yield, safety, purification, analytical checkpoints and material efficiency.
Choose chemoselective and stereoselective transformations and protecting-group strategies.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Organometallic Chemistry
decks.description: Explain and design molecular catalytic cycles.

includes: Metal-carbon bonding and electron counting
Elementary organometallic steps and catalytic-cycle kinetics

practice: Propose and test a catalytic cycle against rate, labeling and product-selectivity evidence.

outcomes.description: Derive catalytic rate predictions and distinguish resting states, inhibition and deactivation.
Construct oxidative addition, insertion, elimination and related elementary catalytic steps.
Analyze metal-carbon bonding, ligand effects and electron counts in organometallic complexes.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Polymer Chemistry
decks.description: Relate macromolecular synthesis to distributions and properties.

includes: Step/chain-growth and controlled polymerization
Molecular-weight distributions, conformation and thermal/mechanical characterization

practice: Analyze polymerization conversion and molecular-weight data and justify a characterization plan.

outcomes.description: Derive number/weight averages and elementary molecular-weight distributions from polymerization models.
Interpret size-exclusion, thermal and mechanical measurements using locally taught chain-conformation models.
Construct polymerization mechanisms and relate reaction conditions to architecture and conversion.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Quantum Chemistry
decks.description: Derive molecular bonding models from quantum mechanics.

includes: Born-Oppenheimer separation, molecular orbitals and variational matrix methods
Antisymmetry, mean-field electronic structure and molecular symmetry

practice: Solve small orbital eigenproblems and compare quantum predictions with qualitative bonding rules.

outcomes.description: Derive variational and antisymmetrized mean-field approximations and identify correlation error.
Construct molecular-orbital Hamiltonian matrices and explain bonding under Born-Oppenheimer separation.
Classify point-group symmetry and construct symmetry-adapted orbital combinations using locally taught representations.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Structural Spectroscopy
decks.description: Infer molecular structure from complementary spectra.

includes: Routine IR, mass spectrometry and one/two-dimensional NMR
Integrated molecular structure elucidation

practice: Elucidate unknown structures from supplied IR, MS and NMR datasets and defend alternative exclusions.

outcomes.description: Reconcile orthogonal spectral constraints and identify unresolved structural ambiguity.
Assign chemical shifts, integration, coupling and basic correlation spectra using locally taught spin rules.
Infer functional groups, mass and fragmentation constraints using locally taught IR/MS signal models.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Thermodynamics
decks.description: Derive macroscopic chemical equilibrium relations.

includes: Thermodynamic identities, chemical potentials and Maxwell relations
Phase equilibria, activities and chemical equilibrium

practice: Derive phase diagrams and test activity models against supplied equilibrium data.

outcomes.description: Derive equilibrium constants and their temperature/pressure dependence from free energy.
Calculate phase equilibria and nonideal solution behavior using chemical potentials and activities.
Derive thermodynamic differential identities and transform between state potentials.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Algorithm Design and Analysis
decks.description: Design algorithms with defensible guarantees.

includes: Correctness, asymptotic and amortized analysis
Divide-and-conquer, greedy, dynamic programming, graph and randomized methods

practice: Implement competing solutions, prove their invariants and test constructed worst cases.

outcomes.description: Prove correctness and derive worst-case and amortized resource bounds.
Design and distinguish greedy, divide-and-conquer and dynamic-programming solutions.
Implement and justify shortest-path, spanning-tree and flow algorithms.
Analyze expected performance and failure probability of elementary randomized algorithms.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Artificial Intelligence
decks.description: Construct agents that search, reason and decide.

includes: Heuristic search and constraint satisfaction
Logical knowledge representation and planning
Bayesian networks, utilities and finite decision processes

practice: Build a planning agent and compare heuristic and uncertainty-aware decisions on controlled tasks.

outcomes.description: Implement heuristic search and constraint propagation and assess completeness and optimality.
Encode knowledge and planning problems and derive solutions using locally taught logical inference.
Compute Bayesian-network inference and finite-horizon expected-utility policies.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Compilers
decks.description: Translate languages into executable representations.

includes: Lexing, parsing and syntax trees
Intermediate representations, dataflow optimization and code generation

practice: Build an end-to-end compiler and differential-test it against an interpreter.

outcomes.description: Generate machine code with calling conventions and register allocation for a small language.
Build intermediate representations and implement sound local and dataflow optimizations.
Construct lexical and parsing machinery and diagnose grammar ambiguity.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Computational Complexity
decks.description: Classify intrinsic computational difficulty.

includes: Time/space complexity, NP completeness and hierarchies
Randomized classes and approximation limits

practice: Write reductions and analyze an approximation algorithm alongside its hardness boundary.

outcomes.description: Derive approximation guarantees and explain reduction-based inapproximability boundaries.
Prove completeness using polynomial reductions and distinguish decision, search and optimization.
Compare time, space and randomized classes and prove standard containment results.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Languages and Computability
decks.description: Characterize what formal machines can compute.

includes: Finite/pushdown automata and formal grammars
Turing machines, universal computation and undecidability

practice: Construct automata and complete reduction proofs for unfamiliar decision problems.

outcomes.description: Convert regular-language representations and analyze context-free grammars and pushdown machines.
Prove undecidability using mapping reductions and diagonalization.
Construct machine simulations and explain universal computation and encodings.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Computer Organization
decks.description: Connect programs to digital machines.

includes: Binary arithmetic, Boolean logic and sequential circuits
Instruction sets, datapaths, caches and pipelines

practice: Use a logic simulator to build a small processor and hand-trace cache accesses.

outcomes.description: Construct combinational and sequential circuits from truth tables and finite-state specifications.
Encode integers and floating-point values and trace assembly through a basic datapath.
Predict cache and pipeline behavior and quantify memory-related performance limits.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Computer Vision
decks.description: Infer scene properties from images.

includes: Image formation, convolution, scale and features
Camera geometry, robust estimation and visual recognition

practice: Build a calibrated two-view reconstruction and evaluate a recognition model on shifted images.

outcomes.description: Estimate camera geometry and reconstruct simple scenes using calibration, correspondences and robust fitting.
Implement image filtering, feature extraction and multiscale representations with sampling analysis.

practiceNotes: This is a proposed curriculum. Completion of flashcard review does not certify proof, programming, laboratory or professional competence.
Use spaced retrieval for definitions, representations, assumptions, mechanisms and method selection; assess derivations, code, data analysis and experimental decisions separately with unseen tasks.
Programming work requires executable environments, version control and reproducible data/provenance records; benchmark claims require stated hardware and workloads.

Chemical, biological, electrical, laser and radiation experiments require appropriate facilities, supervision, risk assessment and institutional authorization. These conditions are not represented as already satisfied.
Use nonpathogenic teaching strains and nonhazardous substitutes where appropriate. Pathogen, animal, human-participant and genetic-engineering work requires relevant ethics and biosafety review.
Security exercises are restricted to owned or explicitly authorized sandbox systems. Robotics and control projects require physical safeguards or simulation.
Fieldwork requires permits where applicable, humane sampling, ecological impact controls and documented location/privacy practices.

Provided scientific software may support method use, but students must still justify assumptions, inspect diagnostics and distinguish supplied algorithms from implementations they can independently construct.
